blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Whole-slide visual question answering (VQA) offers a natural-language interface to pathology, allowing diagnostic and phenotypic questions to be answered directly from tissue slides. However, current vision-language models (VLMs) rely heavily on linguistic priors: their answers are sensitive to the order of the candidate answers, and can be reached through shortcuts that bypass the tissue evidence. To address these challenges, we introduce SlideJev, a framework that separately verifies candidate answers against the slide and learns to ground these judgments in tissue evidence. To connect parallel candidate evaluation with visual evidence learning, we adopt Jev and score each candidate by the difference between support and rejection log-likelihoods from the original language-model head. We compute these scores in parallel using separate prompts with the same format and no option-position labels, then normalize them for answer selection. To ground these scores in tissue evidence, candidate-conditioned reading and comparison guide gated updates to visual tokens across decoder layers. With the backbone frozen, we train these visual modules through the same scores using question-answer and paired-image supervision. Across three whole-slide pathology VQA benchmarks, SlideJev achieves the highest mean overall accuracy and 100% answer consistency across four option orders. Image-control experiments further show that SlideJev achieves the largest average accuracy gains from correct images over mismatched and image-free inputs across the three datasets. Our code is publicly available at https://github.com/leowu-ai/SlideJev.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Pathological decision-making relies on interpreting cellular
morphology and tissue architecture in hematoxylin and eosin
(H&E) whole-slide images (WSIs) to support diagnosis and
phenotypic assessment [ 14 ] .
Whole-slide visual question answering (VQA) provides a
natural-language interface to this process, predicting
an answer from a WSI and a pathology-related
question [ 3 , 13 ] .
A common form is multiple-choice VQA, where the model
selects among candidate diagnostic or phenotypic
interpretations [ 15 ] .
However, pathology questions span diverse medical concepts,
and the relevant visual findings vary with what is being asked.
Answering them requires understanding medical language,
recognizing morphological patterns, and relating these
patterns to the diagnostic or phenotypic concepts expressed
in the question.

These requirements motivate the use of vision-language
models (VLMs), which connect visual representations
with language understanding for pathology question
answering [ 15 , 23 ] .
When applied to WSIs through thumbnails or selected tissue
images, Image-level VLMs face limitations in
morphological detail or tissue coverage [ 3 ] .
By comparison, Whole-slide VLMs incorporate tissue representations
from across the slide, providing access to information
beyond individual image fields [ 24 , 5 ] .
They use the visual context alongside the question
and candidate descriptions to predict an answer.
Despite richer visual context, Conventional VLM (shown in Fig 1 (a)) still face
two reliability challenges when evaluating candidate
answers in multiple-choice VQA. i) Option-order Sensitivity. When candidates are presented jointly, their positions
become part of the prompt context [ 34 , 18 ] .
Reordering them can change the selected answer even
when the question and slide remain unchanged. ii) Visual Evidence Underutilization. Access to whole-slide information does not ensure that
candidate judgments respond to relevant tissue
findings [ 13 , 8 ] .
Prediction accuracy may change little when the slide
is replaced with a mismatched one or removed.

blocks.en:
To support stable pathological decisions grounded in
tissue evidence, we introduce SlideJev , a pathology
VQA framework following the whole-slide VLM paradigm,
as illustrated in Fig. 1 (b).
Overall, we construct a Jev Decision Interface with comparable candidate scores for answer selection
and visual evidence learning.
To reduce option-order sensitivity, we verify candidates
separately through Parallel Candidate Inputs in a shared prompt format without option-position labels,
enabling order-stable selection through Jev.
To ground these assessments in tissue evidence, we then
introduce Gated Visual Injection , using
candidate-relevant evidence and response comparisons
on shared regions to guide visual updates.
The same Jev scores supervise these updates, encouraging
candidate preferences to respond to tissue evidence.
We evaluate SlideJev on the TCGA subset of
SlideBench-VQA [ 3 ] and assess transfer on BCNB [ 30 ] and BRACS-3 [ 2 ] .
SlideJev achieves the highest four-order mean overall
accuracy among the compared methods on all three benchmarks.
Our contributions are summarized as follows: • We present SlideJev, a whole-slide pathology VQA
framework that uses Jev as a shared basis for candidate
selection and visual evidence learning. • We formulate parallel candidate inputs that preserve
verification contexts under option reordering and
combine separate assessments through a common Jev
readout for order-stable answer selection. • We develop gated visual injection that integrates
discriminative tissue evidence with Jev-based supervision
to strengthen image-dependent candidate judgments.

blocks.en:
We present SlideJev , a whole-slide pathology VQA
framework that connects independent candidate verification
with visual evidence learning, as illustrated in Fig. 2 .
Following the whole-slide VLM paradigm, we organize the
decision pipeline around parallel candidate inputs,
gated visual injection, and a Jev readout.
First, we construct Parallel Candidate Inputs by pairing each candidate with the same question and
shared visual prefix without option-position labels,
preserving its verification context under option reordering.
Next, candidate-conditioned reads retrieve evidence from
the shared patch memory, while cross-candidate comparison
evaluates differences in responses to shared tissue patches.
The retrieved evidence and comparison signals are
incorporated through Gated Visual Injection across decoder layers to refine candidate assessment.
Finally, the Jev Readout contrasts support and
rejection log-likelihoods from the original language-model
head, yielding candidate scores that are jointly normalized
for answer selection.
During training, question-answer and paired-image supervision
optimize the visual modules through the same scores,
encouraging candidate preferences to reflect image content
while keeping the pretrained backbone fixed.

Datasets And Tasks. We evaluate SlideJev on SlideBench-VQA [ 3 ] for whole-slide multiple-choice question answering and assess transfer on BCNB [ 30 ] for whole-slide question answering and on BRACS [ 2 ] for diagnostic classification.
Training uses multiple-choice examples from SlideChat’s instruction-tuning dataset, SlideInstruction [ 3 ] , supplementary samples from GTEx [ 27 ] , and image pairs constructed from report-derived labels.

blocks.en: 6 Related Work
blocks.zh: 6 相关工作

blocks.en:
Pathology Vision-language Models. PathVQA introduced question answering over pathology
images [ 10 ] .
Image-level models, including MedDr, MedGemma, and
Quilt-LLaVA, adapt visual-language learning to medical
and pathology images [ 9 , 22 , 23 ] .
Related efforts strengthen pathology-specific image-text
alignment and instruction learning [ 15 , 26 , 25 ] .
However, thumbnails and selected image fields provide
limited tissue detail or coverage for whole-slide questions.
Pathology encoders and slide representation models provide
foundations for broader tissue understanding through
self-supervised and multimodal learning [ 14 , 31 , 32 , 24 , 5 ] .
Building on whole-slide representations, SlideChat supports
gigapixel WSI understanding through instruction
learning [ 3 ] , while WSI-LLaVA emphasizes
morphological findings to explain its answers [ 13 ] .
ALPaCA combines question-dependent visual-text interaction
with tissue prototypes [ 6 ] , and PRISM2
uses clinical dialogue supervision for slide-level
inference [ 29 ] .
SlideJev follows this paradigm while focusing on
stable candidate verification and discriminative visual
evidence use.

blocks.en: 7 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 7 结论

blocks.en:
We presented SlideJev, a whole-slide pathology VQA framework
combining parallel candidate verification and gated visual injection.
Independent, identically formatted prompts without
option-position labels preserve verification contexts
under reordering.
A shared Jev readout connects answer selection with
visual evidence learning.
Question-answer and paired-image supervision train the
visual modules through these scores, with the backbone frozen.
Across SlideBench-VQA, BCNB, and BRACS-3, SlideJev achieves
leading four-order mean overall accuracy among the compared
methods, consistent candidate selection across option orders,
and stronger dependence on the correct slide.
By connecting order-stable candidate verification with
tissue evidence learning through a shared Jev interface,
SlideJev supports reliable pathological decisions grounded
in relevant, slide-specific morphological findings
that inform both diagnostic and phenotypic assessment.
